name: FedLN
title: Labeling Chaos to Learning Harmony: Federated Learning with Noisy Labels
tagline: Learning together when labels cannot be trusted
summary: Federated clients have different amounts of label noise and different computational budgets. FedLN estimates noise on each client and offers three ways to limit its influence: correcting labels before training, adding adaptive knowledge distillation during local learning, or adjusting server aggregation to place more weight on reliable updates.

figure.alt: Three alternative FedLN interventions shown side by side: Nearest Neighbor Correction at initialization, Adaptive Knowledge Distillation during local training, and noise-aware averaging at server aggregation. The alternatives are not a sequential pipeline.
figure.caption: FedLN offers three alternative ways to handle noisy labels, chosen to suit client resources: correct labels before training, guide local training with a teacher, or reduce the influence of noisier client updates during aggregation.
figure.source_label: Explanatory schematic based on the paper

method.title: Correct before training
method.text: Nearest Neighbor Correction uses a pre-trained model to embed local examples. A vote among nearby examples identifies label mismatches and replaces their labels before federated training.

method.title: Guide local learning
method.text: Adaptive Knowledge Distillation adds supervision from a teacher when a client’s estimated noise exceeds a threshold. This helps the local model learn without relying only on its noisy labels.

method.title: Weight the aggregation
method.text: For devices with less compute, NA-FedAvg estimates noise using energy scores in a single federated round. The server then reduces the contribution of updates from noisier clients.

findings.title: Robustness across tasks
findings.text: Experiments on vision and audio classification show improved recognition under synthetic label noise. The three approaches provide different trade-offs between noise handling, local computation, and available pre-trained representations.

findings.title: Human annotation errors
findings.text: Evaluation on CIFAR-10N and CIFAR-100N extends the study to real human label errors. Adaptive distillation is especially effective on the harder CIFAR-100N task when longer federated training is available.

abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm that enables learning models from decentralized private datasets where the labeling effort is entrusted to the clients. While most existing FL approaches assume high-quality labels are readily available on users’ devices, in reality, label noise can naturally occur in FL and is closely related to clients’ characteristics. Due to scarcity of available data and significant label noise variations among clients in FL, existing state-of-the-art centralized approaches exhibit unsatisfactory performance, whereas prior FL studies rely on excessive on-device computational schemes or additional clean data available on the server. We propose FedLN, a framework to deal with label noise across different FL training stages, namely FL initialization, on-device model training, and server model aggregation, able to accommodate the diverse computational capabilities of devices in an FL system. Specifically, FedLN computes per-client noise level estimation in a single federated round and improves the models’ performance by either correcting or mitigating the effect of noisy samples. Our evaluation on various publicly available vision and audio datasets demonstrates a 22% improvement on average compared to other existing methods for a label noise level of 60%. We further validate the efficiency of FedLN in human-annotated real-world noisy datasets and report a 4.8% increase on average in models’ recognition performance, highlighting that FedLN can be useful for improving FL services provided to everyday users.

secondary_figure.alt: NA-FedAvg sends client model updates to a central server, with an additional energy-score path for one-time estimation of each client’s label noise.
secondary_figure.caption: The lightweight NA-FedAvg route: estimate each client’s noise level once, then use that estimate to weight its contribution to the global model. FedLN also offers label correction and adaptive distillation.
